content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me the gap between where you are and the pot is smaller than it probably feels.

Your ≈£1,450/mo free cash is real headroom. The goal needs ≈£170/mo — ≈6% of take-home — which is well within reach. The problem isn't the goal, it's that ≈£1,200/mo of that free cash is currently unaccounted for. That drift is where the move lives.

Set up a standing transfer of ≈£300/mo on payday — about half the drift, so it doesn't bite into family spending or anything that matters. At that pace, the pot lands in ≈3 months instead of ≈10.

You called the ≈£1,200/mo drift unsure — that's the honest answer when you're working from estimates. A real month settles it: either the money is going somewhere specific and you'll see it, or it's genuinely leaking and you'll know what to address.

Checking a real month does two things. It swaps every ≈ for an actual number — estimate against reality, side by side. And the habits half of this picture is still completely empty: timing, what recurs, what spikes. Estimates can't see any of that. Only real transactions can.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
